messages:
julia: Hey folks — quick review please. I iterated on a compact legend for the latency heatmap where p95, p99, and a tiny sampling control live inline. Prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/latency-compact-legend
omar: Nice density. My main worry is discoverability on touch devices. If the sampling control is icon-only at small widths, will users know it exists?
nyla: agree re: touch. Maybe show icon-only at <420px but make the hit area large and open a large tap target popover (not tooltip) with the copy and actions.
glen: microcopy: the inline label currently says "Share latency samples" which might scare legal. Suggest "Share anonymized latency data" and add a short privacy note in the popover: "No request bodies or PII."
julia: good call. was trying to keep it short in-legend: 2 words max. thinking "Share latency" or even "Samples". Which reads clearer next to p95?
omar: "Share latency" is clearer to product folks, but non-technical users might misinterpret. "Samples" is too abstract. If space allows, "Share latency" then tooltip/popover explains.
rowan: accessibility: any inline control must be focusable and have aria-pressed if it's a toggle. For the popover use role="dialog" and trap focus. Also, when the sampling rate changes announce via aria-live: "Sampling rate updated to 1 in 200."
nyla: Implementation note: show current sample rate in the popover: "Sampling: 1 in 200 (~10k events/mo)". We should fetch an estimate from backend for that number. Also include a disabled state if org telemetry is off.
glen: product question: per-project or org-level toggle? The UI copy should match the scope: "for this project" vs "for your org". Product to confirm.
julia: I'll flag product. A/B idea: test two placements — inline compact legend vs stacked control below the heatmap — metric = time-to-find sampling control for new users. Thoughts?
omar: A/B makes sense. Also consider a third variant that uses a floating toolbar on focus (helps keyboard users).
rowan: a11y nit: color contrast for the inline text over the heatmap needs to be 4.5:1. If the heatmap color is saturated, add a subtle backdrop or use a stroke. Also ensure focus ring is visible over busy backgrounds.
nyla: motion: when p95 line toggles, animate opacity only and respect prefers-reduced-motion. Avoid layout shifts when popover opens — use transform+opacity.
glen: copy inside popover (draft): "Sends anonymized latency samples (no request bodies or PII). Sampling: 1 in 200. Learn more." Keep the 'Learn more' link to privacy page. Popover should open on hover/focus and tap.
julia: good. For small screens: icon-only legend item, tap opens full-screen sheet with the same copy + settings slider. Avoid sliders in tiny popovers.
omar: analytics: emit events like ui.heatmap.sampling.toggle and ui.heatmap.sampling.open with attributes {rate, scope, source: legend|toolbar}. Engineering can map these.
rowan: keyboard shortcuts: suggest "K" to toggle p95 visibility when chart focused, and "L" to toggle sampling popover. Add hints in the tooltip/toolbar and document in global shortcuts modal.
nyla: dev note: ensure popover content is reachable by screen readers; use aria-describedby on trigger and id on popover content. For the estimation number, include aria-live polite for updates.
glen: privacy/legal: add an explicit line in popover: "Data is aggregated and cannot be traced back to users." Product/legal to confirm exact phrasing.
julia: Next steps: I'll update Figma with popover + fullscreen sheet for mobile, change microcopy to "Share anonymized latency data", add aria snippets, and create the A/B test brief. Anyone volunteering to review the dev ticket for focus/aria patterns?
rowan: I'll take dev review. I'll also run a quick contrast pass and provide token suggestions for backdrop.
access-bot: Accessibility checklist added: focusable triggers, role=dialog for popovers, aria-pressed for toggle, aria-live for rate changes, prefers-reduced-motion respected, contrast verification.
julia: Thanks all — I'll push the files and ping eng once the ticket is up :sparkles:
